paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His promises, and He keeps them on His own schedule, not ours. Abraham didn't own "a foot of ground" and had no child, yet God promised the land to him and his descendants (Acts 7:5). Joseph got sold by jealous brothers, but "God was with him" (Acts 7:9). Moses spent forty years in Midian before the burning bush (Acts 7:23, 30). Waiting did not mean God had stopped working.

Now look at the other thread, because Stephen is pulling it on purpose. Over and over, God's people turned away the very person God sent to save them. The brothers sold Joseph. Israel pushed Moses aside with "Who made you ruler and judge over us?" (Acts 7:27). Then Stephen says that same Moses is the one God sent "to be their ruler and redeemer" (Acts 7:35). I think Stephen wants the council to hear that pattern loud and clear, and he lets the story do the talking.

So what does that mean for you, baker? God's work often shows up in ways people don't recognize right away, so don't judge it by the first reaction. Hold on to what He says, even when the road runs long and the ground isn't yours yet. And keep your heart turned toward Him, because the people who made a calf were "rejoicing in the works of their hands" (Acts 7:41) and missed the God who brought them out. Stephen's not finished, though, so keep your oven warm.
